A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendix I.

before.justification: V1 reports original sequential-detection experiments, including rejection times and false-positive rates over 1,000 runs, in Section 4 and Appendices G–H.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on initialization sample counts and heterogeneous text streams in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The score functions, betting wealth updates, ONS updates, and composite-testing procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 makes the hint-bound requirement explicit, but v1 already states that requirement in Section 3.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds streams combining three LLM generators and streams mixing human-written and LLM-generated texts. These extend the input scenarios using existing sources; the Olympic news, XSum, WritingPrompts, and PubMedQA coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figures 4 and 7 retain both permutation-test baselines: constant significance level and batch-wise correction using α/2^i. The same ten score-function configurations remain; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds a 20-sample initialization condition with testing beginning at t = 21. Its new mixture protocols use 100 Gemini-1.5-Pro, 200 Gemini-1.5-Flash, and 200 PaLM 2 texts, or 200 human texts and 300 PaLM 2 texts. Existing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 11 adds a targeted comparison of 10 versus 20 initialization samples. Figure 12 adds robustness checks for mixed generators and mixed authorship. The earlier parameter-estimation and cross-domain analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 repeated runs and averaged rejection times and false-positive rates. V2 introduces no new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 11b adds results showing better false-positive control and generally faster detection with 20 initialization samples. Figures 12a–b add rejection-time and false-positive results for heterogeneous streams. Results in Figures 2–10 and Tables 1–12 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, regret and wealth bounds, and proof arguments are retained. Appendix D receives index-notation cleanup. The apparent indicator-symbol typesetting error in Appendix E does not constitute a revised mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit claim that the method avoids tuning an offline affinity-score classification threshold. The abstract and central claims concerning false-positive control, asymptotic power, and expected detection time remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix I broadens the applicability discussion to heterogeneous streams and asserts that mixed-LLM streams preserve the existing guarantees. It interprets longer initialization as improving parameter estimation. The earlier limitations concerning score functions and estimated bounds remain.

D1.justification: V1 specifies generation from a 30-token news prefix. Appendix G in v2 additionally identifies the T5 tokenizer and supplies the generation prompt requesting about 150 words. This is newly disclosed construction detail, not evidence that the dataset was regenerated.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against social-bot detection in the introduction, discussion of Kobak et al.'s excess-vocabulary approach in Appendix A.1, and additional betting literature in Appendix A.2. These broaden the context without replacing the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introduction, flattens the experimental subsection hierarchy, renames Section 5 from Limitations and Outlooks to Conclusion while retaining its limitations, and adds acknowledgments. Other edits mainly refine wording and notation.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, figure placement and captions are revised, and Figures 11–12 are added; Figure 11a redisplays Figure 3a. V2 also introduces a local typesetting defect: indicator functions appear as infinity symbols in Appendix E, including Eq. (41).

improvement.justification: Appendix I supplies useful evidence on initialization and mixed-source detection, while Appendix G improves reproducibility through tokenizer and prompt details. These limited gains outweigh the local indicator-symbol typesetting regression in Appendix E. The central results and existing limitations of estimated score bounds remain.
